messages.author: 5c009c55dafaeed0
messages.subject: mapping abundance predictions
parts:
Dear List,

I'm using pcountOpen to model abundance of six prey species, and I'd
like to make a map showing the spatially referenced abundance
predictions, and another showing the SEs, if possible. I read the help
document on "Modeling and mapping species distributions" from March
29, 2012, and it suggests that the predict function can be used with a
raster stack as the newdata input, and will output rasters showing the
parameter of interest, the SEs, and the confidence intervals. When I
try the predict function on a raster stack, however, I get an error:

> test <- predict(fm52, type="lambda", newdata=the.stack)
Error in .local(object, ...) :
newdata should be a data.frame or inherit unmarkedFrame class

Can anyone tell me if I'm using the predict function wrong, or if it
doesn't work the same for pcountOpen? Is there a better way to make
spatial predictions from pcountOpen models?

Thanks!

Lucretia

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] mapping abundance predictions
parts:
Hi Lucretia,

Are you using version 0.9-7? What do you get when you type:

packageVersion("unmarked")

And does your raster object have class "RasterStack"? Try this:

class(the.stack)

Richard

messages.subject: Re: mapping abundance predictions

Hi Richard,

Thanks for replying. I was using version 0.9-6, so an update to 0.9-7
seems to have helped. I still get an error though:

Error: cannot allocate vector of size 1.1 Gb

I think this means my raster layers are too big for R to deal with,

abundance and standard errors? My model includes both site and
observation covariates.

Thanks so much for your help,

Lucretia

Hi Lucretia,

I had that problem when I predicted for 41 Thousand pixel, so I simply broke that prediction data set into four chunks and predicted for each separately. This worked fine.

Regards -- Marc
